title: Strategic leadership and stakeholder management for DISOs
summary: Use the DISO's advisory role to connect secure information handling with public outcomes, negotiate practical decisions and sustain an accountable improvement programme across organisational boundaries.
outcomes: Build a prioritised security roadmap tied to service outcomes and evidence.
Present a balanced resource case with delivery and operating consequences.
Engage stakeholders according to their authority, needs and dependencies.
Lead a cross-functional decision and handover without overstating evidence or assuming another role's authority.

realExample.title: Home Affairs extends access through banking partners
realExample.documentedOutcome: In its 3 August 2026 statement, Home Affairs reported Smart ID services through 372 participating bank branches and more than half a million applications through the Digital Partnership launched in March 2026.
realExample.discussion: The delivered access channel illustrates the scale that public-service and private-sector cooperation can achieve. Examine the governance of a shared service, its public purpose and the responsibilities that remain with each participant.
realExample.scope: The source reports service reach and applications. It is not a security audit of the partnership or evidence that every application had completed successfully.

units.title: Turn risk advice into a service roadmap
objectives: Frame security priorities in the department's mandate and actual risk.
Compare initiatives using dependencies, resource needs and intended outcomes.
Prepare a roadmap with accountable decisions and review points.

chapters.title: Lead from the public purpose
chapters.bodyHtml:
The DISO's strategic contribution is to help the department make trustworthy information decisions in pursuit of its mandate. Begin with the public outcome: a benefit reaches an eligible resident, a permit is decided fairly, a record can be found and explained, or a critical service remains available. Describe how a security weakness threatens that outcome and how an improvement would protect it.

Separate obligations, risks and aspirations. An applicable directive creates a requirement; an observed weakness creates a risk or implementation problem; a new technology may create an opportunity. Put each on its proper basis. Do not present every preferred tool as mandatory or allow an attractive innovation to erase an existing obligation. Explain uncertainty where evidence is incomplete, and obtain the relevant professional advice when an authority question affects the decision.

Use the institution's established planning and governance processes. The DISO should influence service design, procurement, operations and review early enough to change the outcome. A security comment made only after a major contract is signed has less practical scope. Build working relationships with service owners, GITO, enterprise risk, finance, HR, procurement, records management and the Information Officer without merging their distinct accountabilities.

chapters.title: Prioritise a programme, not a shopping list
chapters.bodyHtml:
A useful roadmap groups work around service improvements and dependencies. 'Buy a new monitoring platform' is an activity. 'Bring the critical-service estate into a defined monitored scope, provide an on-call response and demonstrate a usable escalation' describes the operating result. The platform may support that result, but ownership, configuration, staffing and service coverage are also required.

Compare initiatives using their contribution to obligations, public-service impact, current exposure, feasibility, dependency order, cost and the time needed for benefit. Avoid an unexplained composite score that hides a mandatory dependency. A low-cost access inventory may be essential before a more expensive privileged-access project can be scoped. A recovery improvement may depend on a supplier contract or a separate identity design.

Give the programme phases and decision points. Immediate work can contain a known exposure; the next phase can repair a process and demonstrate the result; later work can replace a fragile architecture. Each phase needs an owner, resources, dependencies and acceptance conditions. Keep the original reason for the priority visible so management can reassess the programme when the service, threat or budget changes.

chapters.title: Make the resource case complete
chapters.bodyHtml:
An investment case should compare feasible options, including the consequence of deferral. Describe acquisition, implementation, staff time, training, operating cost, integration, exit and maintenance where material. A cheap purchase can become expensive if the department cannot operate it; a higher initial cost may still be justified by a service benefit, but the case needs a credible basis.

State the intended benefit and how it will be observed. Reducing recovery time from an observed six hours toward an approved four-hour objective is measurable. 'Eliminate all cyber risk' is not a credible outcome. Distinguish an estimate from an observed result and record key assumptions, such as staff availability or a supplier's supported interface. A business case can be decisive without promising certainty.

Ask for a clear management decision: approve the stated phase and resources, select an option, defer with conditions, or seek a revised proposal. Name the authority and the date the decision is needed. Link the later review to the original assumptions and intended service result. This lets management stop, adjust or continue an investment on evidence rather than on sunk cost alone.

application.title: A ninety-day security programme for a public service
application.instructionsHtml:
Allow about 60 minutes. The fictional Ndlovu department processes 10,000 assistance applications a week. Its access inventory is incomplete, staff use ad hoc spreadsheet exports for appeals, and the last complete recovery took six hours against an approved four-hour objective. A supplier identity contract expires in nine months. Management can allocate R650,000 and two staff equivalents over the next ninety days; a proposed R3.2 million platform replacement cannot finish in that period.

Design a ninety-day programme and an outline for the following year. Include immediate protection, process repair, measurable service results, dependencies and a resource decision. Compare the platform replacement with improvements that can be completed now, without assuming that cost alone determines the better long-term option.
application.deliverable: A phased roadmap, a resource comparison and a one-page management decision request.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
A sound first phase establishes service and access ownership, identifies critical privileges and contains known inappropriate access through the approved process. It also replaces ad hoc appeal exports with a controlled information-handling route and clarifies the records and privacy responsibilities. The goal is useful service protection, not merely completion of an inventory.

The next phase tests and repairs the complete recovery dependency that caused the six-hour result, including identity and service validation. Define an acceptance condition against the approved objective and retain any remaining limitation. Start the identity-contract decision early enough to evaluate continuity, exit and procurement lead times before expiry.

Use the ninety-day budget for a feasible combination with named staff and operating support. Evaluate the larger replacement in the following-year plan against the same service outcomes, integration and lifecycle costs. Ask management to approve the near-term scope and resources, identify the longer-term decision date and agree how the programme will be reviewed. Alternative priorities can be justified if the service impact and obligations are addressed explicitly.

rubric.criterion: Ties priorities to actual service risks and obligations
Sequences dependencies and feasible near-term work
Includes lifecycle resources and a balanced option comparison
Defines decision authority and measurable acceptance

reflection.prompt: Which security proposal would become more persuasive if you described the public-service outcome before the technology?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Rewrite its opening as the affected service, the observed problem, the intended improvement and the decision required.

quiz.title: Turn risk advice into a service roadmap — knowledge check

questions.name: M13-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Which opening best frames a strategic DISO proposal?

answers.textHtml: The service outcome at risk, the observed weakness and the decision needed to improve it.
answers.feedbackHtml: Start with the department's purpose and a concrete decision.

answers.textHtml: The product name and the vendor's market position.
answers.feedbackHtml: Those may be relevant later but do not establish the public-service need.

answers.textHtml: A statement that every new technology is a compliance requirement.
answers.feedbackHtml: Requirements must be tied to their actual authority.

answers.textHtml: A promise that the proposal will remove all future risk.
answers.feedbackHtml: A credible case recognises residual risk and uncertainty.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Start with the department's purpose and a concrete decision.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: What makes a roadmap different from a shopping list?

answers.textHtml: It connects work, dependencies, owners and acceptance conditions to service outcomes.
answers.feedbackHtml: A roadmap explains how the work will produce a useful result.

answers.textHtml: It lists a larger number of products.
answers.feedbackHtml: Volume of purchases does not establish an operating programme.

answers.textHtml: It excludes staff and process work to remain technical.
answers.feedbackHtml: Service results usually depend on people and management as well as technology.

answers.textHtml: It treats every activity as independent so all can begin immediately.
answers.feedbackHtml: Dependencies affect feasibility and sequence.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A roadmap explains how the work will produce a useful result.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: A low-cost access inventory is required to scope a larger privilege-control project. How should it be prioritised?

answers.textHtml: As a necessary dependency, with its own useful output and owner.
answers.feedbackHtml: Make necessary dependencies explicit in the programme.

answers.textHtml: Below every higher-cost initiative because expenditure measures importance.
answers.feedbackHtml: Cost is not a measure of dependency or service impact.

answers.textHtml: After the larger project's procurement so the solution is already fixed.
answers.feedbackHtml: That risks buying against an unknown scope.

answers.textHtml: As the final proof that privilege risk has been eliminated.
answers.feedbackHtml: An inventory supports decisions but is not the whole control.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Make necessary dependencies explicit in the programme.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: Which benefit statement is most credible?

answers.textHtml: Demonstrate recovery of the defined critical service within its approved objective after repairing the observed dependency.
answers.feedbackHtml: A benefit should be observable and linked to the original problem.

answers.textHtml: Guarantee that no service disruption can ever occur.
answers.feedbackHtml: That exceeds what a recovery improvement can establish.

answers.textHtml: Buy the selected platform before year-end.
answers.feedbackHtml: A purchase milestone is not the service benefit.

answers.textHtml: Increase the number of security documents regardless of use.
answers.feedbackHtml: Document volume does not establish an operating outcome.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A benefit should be observable and linked to the original problem.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: A proposed tool is inexpensive to buy but needs substantial specialist staffing. What belongs in the decision?

answers.textHtml: The relevant lifecycle costs, operating capacity and feasible alternatives.
answers.feedbackHtml: Compare complete feasible options rather than isolated purchase prices.

answers.textHtml: Only the purchase price because operating costs belong to another year.
answers.feedbackHtml: The department still needs a sustainable operating model.

answers.textHtml: An assumption that existing staff can absorb all work without assessment.
answers.feedbackHtml: Capacity is a material assumption requiring examination.

answers.textHtml: Automatic rejection of every tool with recurring costs.
answers.feedbackHtml: Recurring cost can be justified if the whole case is sound.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Compare complete feasible options rather than isolated purchase prices.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: When should the DISO engage in a major service procurement?

answers.textHtml: Early enough to influence requirements, responsibilities, operating design and exit arrangements.
answers.feedbackHtml: Early cross-functional engagement improves the available choices.

answers.textHtml: Only after the supplier has completed implementation.
answers.feedbackHtml: Late advice has less scope to change important decisions.

answers.textHtml: Instead of the procurement and service owners, taking over all their authority.
answers.feedbackHtml: The DISO contributes within distinct institutional responsibilities.

answers.textHtml: Only when an incident occurs during the contract.
answers.feedbackHtml: Security and continuity needs should inform design and operation before an incident.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Early cross-functional engagement improves the available choices.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which elements make a programme phase ready for management approval? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Named resources, dependencies and an accountable owner.
answers.feedbackHtml: These establish how the work can be delivered.

answers.textHtml: Acceptance conditions tied to the intended service improvement.
answers.feedbackHtml: These establish what completion should demonstrate.

answers.textHtml: An assumption that every supplier promise has already been observed.
answers.feedbackHtml: Promises and verified results are different evidence.

answers.textHtml: A rule that the phase cannot be reconsidered after circumstances change.
answers.feedbackHtml: A responsible programme can adapt through the proper decision process.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A phase needs both a delivery basis and a defined useful result.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which distinctions should a resource case preserve? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: An applicable obligation versus a preferred design choice.
answers.feedbackHtml: They have different authority and flexibility.

answers.textHtml: An estimated benefit versus an observed result.
answers.feedbackHtml: Management needs to understand the evidence behind each claim.

answers.textHtml: All uncertainty can be omitted if it makes the recommendation clearer.
answers.feedbackHtml: Material uncertainty affects the choice.

answers.textHtml: Every completed procurement automatically delivers its intended benefit.
answers.feedbackHtml: Implementation and operation still determine the result.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Clarity includes the basis and limits of the proposal.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A security roadmap should be reassessed when the department's service priorities or material dependencies change.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: A roadmap supports the mandate and actual conditions; it is not an unchangeable list.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. A roadmap supports the mandate and actual conditions; it is not an unchangeable list.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A roadmap supports the mandate and actual conditions; it is not an unchangeable list.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: A proposed investment's sunk cost is sufficient reason to continue it even when the original service benefit is no longer feasible.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Management should review the remaining options and consequences rather than rely only on past expenditure.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Management should review the remaining options and consequences rather than rely only on past expenditure.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Management should review the remaining options and consequences rather than rely only on past expenditure.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match each programme element to its purpose.

pairs.answer: Shows what must be available first or alongside it
Defines the useful result to demonstrate
Allows continuation or adjustment on current evidence

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A coherent programme connects purpose, delivery and accountable learning.

questions.name: M13-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: A strategic proposal begins with the public [[1]] and ends with a specific management [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Purpose and decision make the proposal useful.

units.title: Lead across boundaries and hand over usable work
objectives: Map stakeholder interests and decision rights for a shared service.
Communicate disagreement and uncertainty without overstating authority.
Integrate the course's governance, risk, incident and continuity tools in a practical handover.

chapters.title: Partnership requires explicit responsibilities
chapters.bodyHtml:
The Home Affairs banking-partnership example demonstrates delivered reach through organisations that have different capabilities and responsibilities. A shared public service needs clarity about who operates each step, who decides how information is used, who handles exceptions and how the public obtains help. Cooperation is not achieved by assuming that the strongest technical participant owns every decision.

Map stakeholders by their role in the service, their authority, their information needs and the effect a failure would have on them. Include staff who deliver the service, residents or their representatives, suppliers, the Information Officer, records management, risk and finance. Do not confuse influence with formal authority. A senior or vocal participant may still need another role's approval for a particular action.

Agree the working arrangements: named contacts and alternates, decision routes, service and information boundaries, incident notification, continuity, change review and exit. Make the arrangements usable when an ordinary contact is absent. A contract can define responsibilities, but the parties must also demonstrate that the people and operating routes exist.

chapters.title: Communicate a difficult recommendation
chapters.bodyHtml:
Disagreement is part of useful advice. A service owner may need to meet a deadline while the security team identifies a material weakness. Present the common public purpose first, then the observed problem, the plausible consequences and the available options. Distinguish a fact, an assumption, an estimate and a recommendation. This creates room for a decision without turning the discussion into a contest over technical confidence.

Tailor the detail to the audience while preserving the meaning. A technical team may need a dependency diagram; an executive may need a one-page choice; a resident may need to know how to obtain the service and when the next update will arrive. Use clear language and accessible formats. Do not disclose sensitive operational details merely to make an explanation appear authoritative.

Escalate through the proper route when a decision exceeds delegated authority or a material disagreement remains. Record the advice, the decision, conditions and owner. Do not silently approve on another person's behalf or label an unresolved matter settled. Equally, avoid treating every uncertainty as a reason to halt useful work: identify what can proceed safely, what decision is needed and what evidence would change the recommendation.

chapters.title: Handover is an operating capability
chapters.bodyHtml:
A handover should let the receiving team operate the service and maintain its decisions. Include the approved scope, information and service owners, the current configuration or process, access and support routes, known limitations, incident and continuity arrangements, change history and the records needed for accountability. Protect secret values through the approved custody route rather than embedding them in a general guide.

Ask the receiving team to perform meaningful tasks: find the current policy, use a delegated alternate, trace a source record, manage a scoped access change, interpret a recovery result and resolve an exception. A presentation alone does not establish that the work is usable. Record the actual receiving outcome and repair material gaps in the same operating process.

Close the programme with the appropriate management review and retained ownership. Identify what is complete, which residual issues have owners and when the next review is required. Preserve source material and records under the relevant requirements so the department can update and republish its work. A good DISO leaves a functioning capability and understandable decisions for the next person.

application.title: Capstone: advise the shared application service
application.instructionsHtml:
Allow about 60 minutes. A fictional department and a contracted service provider will open a public application channel in four weeks. The service purpose and responsible business owner are agreed. Data includes identity documents and appeal records. A supplier proposes reusing uploaded documents for unrelated analytics. Privileged access is not fully reviewed. A complete recovery exercise took six hours against a four-hour RTO, while the verified data point met the thirty-minute RPO. The normal incident contact will be unavailable during launch week. The launch team proposes declaring every control green because the database and website work.

Prepare an integrated DISO recommendation using this course. Address legal and policy authority, classification and records, governance, risk and access, architecture dependencies, incident and continuity readiness, staff learning, monitoring and the launch decision. Identify work that can proceed, the decisions required and the full operating handover. You may recommend a phased launch if the scope and conditions are explicit; do not manufacture authority or claim zero residual risk.
application.deliverable: A two-page decision brief, a prioritised action and responsibility table, and a receiving checklist.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Begin with the public service and information purpose. Route the proposed analytics reuse through the appropriate business, privacy and legal assessment rather than treating supplier possession as permission. Confirm applicable classification and records treatment, and preserve the distinct authority of the business owner, Information Officer, GITO, DISO and records function.

Complete the relevant privilege decisions, identify the recovery dependency causing the time miss, appoint the authorised incident alternate and rehearse the launch contact route. Report the recovery-time miss separately from the met recovery-point objective. Train staff on the actual verification, reporting and fallback tasks. Establish a small monitoring view covering critical-service availability, access exceptions, recovery readiness and unresolved decisions.

Present feasible launch choices to the authorised management forum. A phased launch can be reasonable if its reduced scope has demonstrated controls, service capacity, communication and clear conditions for expansion. State what remains to be decided or repaired and who owns it. The receiving handover should include current procedures, support and access routes, data and source ownership, incident and recovery instructions, change records, known limitations and a practical staff walkthrough.

rubric.criterion: Integrates authority, purpose and information handling correctly
Prioritises access, recovery and incident readiness with owners
Makes a balanced launch recommendation using actual results
Provides a usable monitoring, learning and operating handover

reflection.prompt: How would you explain a material disagreement with a service owner while preserving a productive working relationship?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Write a short statement of the shared purpose, the specific observation, the options and the decision route. Separate what you recommend from what you are authorised to decide.

quiz.title: Lead across boundaries and hand over usable work — knowledge check

questions.name: M13-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: A supplier holds copies of uploaded identity documents. Does this alone authorise an unrelated analytics use?

answers.textHtml: No; the proposed purpose and authority require the relevant business, privacy and legal assessment.
answers.feedbackHtml: Assess the specific information purpose and responsibilities.

answers.textHtml: Yes, because possession transfers decision authority.
answers.feedbackHtml: Holding information does not by itself authorise a new purpose.

answers.textHtml: Yes, if the supplier describes the analytics as innovative.
answers.feedbackHtml: A claimed benefit does not establish the applicable authority.

answers.textHtml: No use of any supplier can ever be lawful.
answers.feedbackHtml: The issue is the particular purpose and arrangement, not a blanket prohibition.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Assess the specific information purpose and responsibilities.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A senior stakeholder strongly supports a change outside their delegated authority. What should the DISO do?

answers.textHtml: Engage their concerns and route the decision to the role or forum that actually has authority.
answers.feedbackHtml: Include stakeholders while preserving the real decision rights.

answers.textHtml: Treat seniority as automatic authority over every decision.
answers.feedbackHtml: Influence and delegated authority are not identical.

answers.textHtml: Ignore the stakeholder because they cannot sign the decision.
answers.feedbackHtml: Their operational knowledge and interests may still be relevant.

answers.textHtml: Approve the change personally to prevent delay.
answers.feedbackHtml: The DISO should not assume another role's authority.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Include stakeholders while preserving the real decision rights.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: How should a DISO present a launch disagreement?

answers.textHtml: Start with the shared service purpose, then evidence, consequences, feasible options and the required decision.
answers.feedbackHtml: Clear, proportionate advice supports a productive management decision.

answers.textHtml: State only that security has vetoed the launch, regardless of actual delegation.
answers.feedbackHtml: That may overstate authority and conceal the decision basis.

answers.textHtml: Remove the risk from the report to preserve the relationship.
answers.feedbackHtml: Constructive engagement requires the material issue to remain visible.

answers.textHtml: List every technical detail without a recommendation.
answers.feedbackHtml: The audience still needs a practical choice and advice.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Clear, proportionate advice supports a productive management decision.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: An exercise meets its RPO but misses its RTO. Which launch report is accurate?

answers.textHtml: The verified data-recency objective was met, while the service-recovery time objective was missed.
answers.feedbackHtml: Report distinct results without merging them into a misleading overall claim.

answers.textHtml: Both objectives were met because the database was restored.
answers.feedbackHtml: The two objectives measure different outcomes.

answers.textHtml: Both objectives failed because one failed.
answers.feedbackHtml: Preserve the actual result of each objective.

answers.textHtml: Only the favourable result should appear in the executive report.
answers.feedbackHtml: The time miss may be material to the launch decision.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Report distinct results without merging them into a misleading overall claim.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What is a strong receiving check for an operating handover?

answers.textHtml: The receiving staff perform representative tasks using the supplied procedures and authority routes.
answers.feedbackHtml: A practical receiving task reveals gaps that can be repaired before closure.

answers.textHtml: The author presents the slides without any recipient interaction.
answers.feedbackHtml: A presentation alone does not establish usability.

answers.textHtml: The archive contains a large number of documents.
answers.feedbackHtml: File volume does not show that the recipient can operate the service.

answers.textHtml: The supplier confirms privately that it understands the system.
answers.feedbackHtml: The department needs its own usable capability.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A practical receiving task reveals gaps that can be repaired before closure.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: Some launch work is safe to continue while one material decision remains unresolved. What should the recommendation do?

answers.textHtml: Define the work that can proceed and the exact decision, conditions and owner for the remaining scope.
answers.feedbackHtml: A precise boundary enables progress while preserving the required decision.

answers.textHtml: Halt all unrelated activity whenever any uncertainty exists.
answers.feedbackHtml: That can unnecessarily prevent useful authorised work.

answers.textHtml: Proceed with every part and call the unresolved issue accepted.
answers.feedbackHtml: An unresolved decision is not an accepted risk.

answers.textHtml: Leave the boundary informal so each team can decide later.
answers.feedbackHtml: Unclear scope creates inconsistent actions and accountability.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A precise boundary enables progress while preserving the required decision.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which items belong in a usable operating handover? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Current procedures, owners, support routes and known limitations.
answers.feedbackHtml: These let the receiving team operate and make informed decisions.

answers.textHtml: Incident, continuity and change arrangements with practical access to required records.
answers.feedbackHtml: These support operation beyond the initial launch.

answers.textHtml: Unrestricted secret credentials embedded in a widely distributed guide.
answers.feedbackHtml: Secrets need the approved protected custody route.

answers.textHtml: Only the final presentation, with all source and decision history removed.
answers.feedbackHtml: The department needs maintainable work and relevant records.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Handover should create a sustained operating capability.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which statements about a phased launch are sound? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Its limited scope and expansion conditions should be explicit.
answers.feedbackHtml: This makes the decision and later change understandable.

answers.textHtml: The included service needs demonstrated controls and useful capacity.
answers.feedbackHtml: A phase must still be operable within its chosen scope.

answers.textHtml: Calling a launch a pilot removes every applicable obligation.
answers.feedbackHtml: A label does not suspend relevant requirements.

answers.textHtml: Unresolved risks automatically become accepted when the first user signs in.
answers.feedbackHtml: Acceptance requires the actual authorised decision.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A phase is a deliberate service choice, not a way to erase responsibility.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A stakeholder map should include affected service users and operational staff as well as formal decision-makers.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Different participants supply needs, impact information and operating knowledge even when they do not approve the final decision.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Different participants supply needs, impact information and operating knowledge even when they do not approve the final decision.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Different participants supply needs, impact information and operating knowledge even when they do not approve the final decision.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: The Home Affairs partnership's reported application volume is, by itself, a security audit proving every control effective.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. The source establishes service reach and applications; it does not establish that broader assurance claim.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: The source establishes service reach and applications; it does not establish that broader assurance claim.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The source establishes service reach and applications; it does not establish that broader assurance claim.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match each communication need to the most suitable emphasis.

pairs.answer: Available service, practical access and next update
Usable procedures, support and representative tasks

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Tailor detail to the audience while preserving the meaning.

questions.name: M13-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Constructive advice separates the DISO's [[1]] from the authorised owner's [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Clear roles allow useful advice and accountable action.
